posts.description: Miles submitted this photo with the comment “We are driving between Portland and Reno, and I was just explaining Goths Up Trees to Grace and our driver Vic, and they got super excited. Grace has this photo taken in Texas and would like to submit it for your kind consideration. We obviously don’t expect to be exempt from the rules which they are also very excited about” I’m quite upset that anyone would think they were exempt from the rules, especially when several of the rules have been so flagrantly ignored and the subject of the photo has allegedly expressed excitement multiple times in a single car trip. I feel like it’s time to remind everyone of the things I look for in a photo because it seems clear to me that people are forgetting. Hell, I haven’t posted in so long that I’M forgetting. posts.title: Makala submitted this photo with the comment: “Me and my goth friends took our precious time out of…
posts.description: Makala submitted this photo with the comment: “Me and my goth friends took our precious time out of our day to take a professional goths up trees picture because we LOVE your website. We would love to be a part of it🙏🖤” Is this goth Josie and the Pussycats? Was there sale on wide-net fishnet socks? Why is there a tiny toy guitar? Regardless, I enjoy what’s going on here. We have 4 goths at various levels up a dead tree in a moody forest. No one’s smiling. They’re out in the daylight, but we must assume that they’re mostly out of range of UV rays due to the dappled forest light. White boots give me the ick, as the kids say, and I am genuinely confused by a couple of the outfits, but I think that adds a certain je ne sais quoi to the experience that I appreciate. Bonus points for the number of goths and the professional picture. 4.8 out of 5 - It’s always worth taking precious time out of your day to take a professional goths up trees picture.

posts.title: Janus Herrera submitted these photos with the comment: “For your consideration: Kindly note that we…
posts.description: Janus Herrera submitted these photos with the comment: “For your consideration: Kindly note that we are desert goths, and as such, trees in cemeteries are hard to find. Finding trees that will support three goths at the same time adds a second layer of complexity here, but we have sent you our best. The cemetery visit came after the larger cottonwood tree, so our winged friend had enjoyed some tequila at a local Mexican restaurant in between and declined to make the second ascent. With appreciation for the fine collection you have cultivated and wishes for a witchy 2026!” I think everyone can agree that this is some fine work from these three desert goth friends. I share their pain in trying to locate a decent cemetery with a climbable tree and I don’t even live in a desert, just an ol’ town where cemetery landscaping is predominately extremely maintainable shrubs or small, spindly trees that won’t take the weight of a reasonable sized bird, let alone a reasonable sized goth.
